description: A novel sieve eliminates >99% of candidate numbers from Collatz delay searches using modular arithmetic. By precomputing which residue classes mod 2^k must produce shorter trajectories, we skip directly to numbers whose binary structure forces long odd-step chains.
mathematical_formalization: For sieve width w = 2^k, partition Z into residue classes r mod w. For each r, simulate k steps of the shortcut Collatz map T(n) = (3n+1)/2 if odd, n/2 if even. Discard r if the trajectory drops below r within k steps. Surviving fraction ~ (3/4)^k * correction. With k=32, survival rate < 0.008.
analogical_connections: Sieve of Eratosthenes for composites -> Sieve of Collatz for short trajectories
CPU branch prediction -> trajectory prediction from low-order bits
Restriction enzymes in molecular biology -> cutting search space at modular recognition sites
implementation_hypothesis: Precompute a lookup table of size 2^k mapping each residue class to (steps_taken, resulting_residue, odd_count, even_count). Only iterate numbers where odd_count/even_count > 0.60.
experiment_seed: Compare wall-clock time to find all delay records below 10^12 with sieve widths k=16, 20, 24, 28, 32.
